description: Estimate prior probabilities from occurrence data, habitat, and spatial modeling

functions.name: build_priors
functions.description: High-level wrapper: GBIF fetch -> habitat -> grid -> model -> priors -> backbone translation

inputs.name: taxa
inputs.description: Data frame with taxonomy rank columns. Column names encode the rank (family, genus, species). IMPORTANT: the prior algorithm estimates sampling effort from multiple species captured by similar methods. A single target species is insufficient — provide a broader group (e.g. data.frame(family = 'Gobiidae') or a multi-species list) so the algorithm can gauge how well-sampled each grid cell is.

inputs.name: lat
inputs.description: Latitude of study site

inputs.name: lon
inputs.description: Longitude of study site

inputs.name: rank_system
inputs.description: Taxonomy ranks

inputs.name: habitat_scheme
inputs.description: Habitat classification: NULL (default 3-category: Marine/Freshwater/Terrestrial), 'IUCN_L1' (18 IUCN Level 1 groups), or a custom data.frame with an l1_name column listing the habitat categories (e.g. data.frame(l1_name = c('Estuarine', 'Freshwater', 'Rocky Intertidal', 'Sandy Subtidal'))). If the user provides habitat names, construct a custom data frame.

inputs.name: llm_fn
inputs.description: LLM provider for habitat assignment

inputs.name: geographic_context
inputs.description: Geographic hint for habitat LLM

inputs.name: target_backbone_id
inputs.description: Target backbone for translating prior taxon names (4 = NCBI, 11 = GBIF). Does not affect the GBIF occurrence query itself.

inputs.name: year_range
inputs.description: GBIF year filter as a comma-separated string, e.g. '2000,2024'. NULL (default) returns all years. Must be a string, NOT a numeric vector.

inputs.name: search_radius_deg
inputs.description: Radius in degrees around site for GBIF search. Real function default is 2, but larger values (5-6) provide more grid cells for the spatial model and produce much better species-habitat differentiation -- values below 3 often produce too few grid cells for the model to estimate species-specific habitat slopes, so consider overriding the default upward. (2026-09-07 metadata resync: this entry's own "default" field previously stated 5, silently overriding the real default of 2 rather than describing it -- corrected to match reality, guidance retained.)

inputs.name: supplemental_occurrences
inputs.description: Additional occurrence data to include

inputs.name: verbose
inputs.description: Print progress messages

output.description: List with $priors (data frame with grid_id, main_habitat, taxon_name, theta) and attributes

functions.scaling_note: GBIF + LLM + modeling; 10-60 min depending on taxon count and geographic scope

functions.name: optimize_grid_size
functions.description: Find optimal spatial grid resolution for prior estimation

inputs.name: observation_data
inputs.description: Occurrence data with coordinates

inputs.name: n_covariates
inputs.description: Number of model covariates

inputs.name: lat_col
inputs.description: Latitude column

inputs.name: lon_col
inputs.description: Longitude column

inputs.name: species_col
inputs.description: Species column

inputs.name: habitat_col
inputs.description: Habitat column

functions.name: prepare_model_dataframe
functions.description: Prepare gridded occurrence data for biodiversity model fitting -- computes per-taxon presence/absence and shared effort denominator (n_total_at_site) per grid cell

inputs.name: data
inputs.description: Gridded occurrence data with grid_id, lat_r, lon_r, habitat_col, taxon_name

inputs.name: covariates
inputs.description: Spatial covariate columns

inputs.name: habitat_col
inputs.description: Habitat column; NULL disables habitat modeling

inputs.name: cor_threshold
inputs.description: Drop a covariate if correlated above this with another

inputs.name: sampling_group_col
inputs.description: Column identifying which detection PROCESS/METHOD each row belongs to (e.g. 'fish' vs 'birds' vs 'phytoplankton'). When supplied, n_total_at_site is computed group-aware (split-and-recombine internally) so effort isn't pooled across incomparable sampling processes. NOT the same as a physical site/spatial_group_id

output.description: Data frame ready for compute_moran_basis()/train_biodiversity_model() (or train_biodiversity_model_by_group() when sampling_group_col was supplied)

functions.name: train_biodiversity_model_by_group
functions.description: Fits one biodiversity model PER sampling_group_col value instead of pooling every taxon into one model. Required when data spans multiple detection processes with different effort -- train_biodiversity_model() itself refuses multi-group data

inputs.name: data
inputs.description: Raw gridded occurrence data (NOT pre-processed by prepare_model_dataframe() -- this function re-derives model data per group internally)

inputs.name: formula
inputs.description: Model formula, typically from screen_spatial_formula()$formula run once on the full/combined data

inputs.name: sampling_group_col
inputs.description: Column identifying detection process/method groups. Required -- for ungrouped data use train_biodiversity_model() directly

inputs.name: covariates
inputs.description: Spatial covariate columns

inputs.name: habitat_col
inputs.description: Habitat column

inputs.name: taxon_col
inputs.description: Taxon column

inputs.name: response
inputs.description: 'theta' or 'psi'

inputs.name: min_obs_threshold
inputs.description: Minimum observations to attempt a group fit

inputs.name: effort_threshold
inputs.description: Minimum total effort to attempt a group fit

inputs.name: min_positive_rows
inputs.description: Minimum positive-detection rows to attempt a group fit

output.description: Named list of biofreq_model objects, one per sampling_group_col value. Groups that fail to fit (too sparse) are dropped with a warning, not an error

functions.scaling_note: One model fit per group; seconds to minutes depending on number of groups

functions.name: generate_domestic_food_priors
functions.description: Adds named Beta(alpha, beta) prior rows for domestic/commensal animal species, human food/crop species, and (optionally) candidate cultivated plants -- a non-GBIF prior source using live iNaturalist casual-grade evidence, for the gap where occurrence-database indexing structurally under-counts captive/cultivated organisms. Output is bind_rows()-compatible with generate_full_priors()'s taxaexpect_priors

inputs.name: model_obj
inputs.description: Output of train_biodiversity_model() (or one element of train_biodiversity_model_by_group()'s list); used only for N_total and habitat_col so these rows sit on the same theta scale as the rest of taxaexpect_priors

inputs.name: lat
inputs.description: Query site latitude for the iNaturalist search

inputs.name: lng
inputs.description: Query site longitude for the iNaturalist search

inputs.name: grid_id
inputs.description: Grid cell identifier attached to every output row, for joining into taxaexpect_priors

inputs.name: domestic_animal_taxa
inputs.description: Domestic/commensal animal taxon names. Default is a pre-populated starting list (dog, cat, cow, sheep, pig, chicken, horse, Homo sapiens, etc.). Set to character(0) to disable this channel

inputs.name: food_species_taxa
inputs.description: Human food/crop species taxon names, a separate contamination category from domestic_animal_taxa (food-handling/lab-bench contamination, not pet/livestock). Default is a pre-populated starting list. Set to character(0) to disable

inputs.name: candidate_plant_taxa
inputs.description: Candidate plant-kingdom taxa (e.g. from your study's own plant-kingdom BLAST/GBIF matches) to check for real local cultivated/casual-grade iNaturalist evidence. Default NULL (channel disabled, no live iNaturalist calls made unless supplied)

inputs.name: radius_km
inputs.description: iNaturalist search radius

inputs.name: taxonomy
inputs.description: Optional taxon_name + rank columns (incl. kingdom) joined onto the result. Supplying a kingdom column enables an iNaturalist cross-kingdom-homonym check

inputs.name: api_token
inputs.description: iNaturalist API token; defaults to the INAT_API_TOKEN environment variable

output.description: One row per resolved domestic/food/plant taxon: taxon_name (always populated, unlike generate_undetected_diversity()'s anonymous proxies), grid_id, alpha, beta, theta_mean, theta_sd, model_tier ('tier_domestic_food'), prior_source_type ('domestic_animal'/'food_species'/'domestic_plant'), inat_n_observations_local, inat_kingdom, inat_kingdom_mismatch

functions.scaling_note: iNaturalist API; seconds to ~1 min depending on how many candidate_plant_taxa are supplied

functions.name: calibrate_kernel_bandwidth
functions.description: 2026-09-07, new -- kernel-priors path (2026-08-30/31 redesign), a site-centered distance-kernel alternative to the GLMM/grid-cell prediction path (dist_to_priors.R). Selects the kernel bandwidth (lambda_km, and optionally a covariate bandwidth) via leave-one-block-out composition prediction -- replaces the GLMM path's AIC formula screening. Offline, no network calls, seconds.

inputs.name: occurrence_data
inputs.description: Standardized occurrence data with lat/lon/main_habitat/taxon_name columns (std_occurrences)

inputs.name: site_habitat
inputs.description: Focal habitat to restrict the calibration/estimation to (e.g. 'Marine')

inputs.name: lambda_grid
inputs.description: Candidate bandwidths (km) to try

inputs.name: covariate_col
inputs.description: Optional numeric covariate column (e.g. 'depth_m') for a second, covariate-space kernel factor

inputs.name: lambda_covariate_grid
inputs.description: Candidate covariate bandwidths, only used when covariate_col is supplied

inputs.name: block_size_deg
inputs.description: Spatial block size (degrees) for the leave-one-block-out cross-validation

inputs.name: min_block_records
inputs.description: Minimum records a block needs to be scored

output.description: $best (the chosen lambda_km/lambda_covariate + its LOBO loss), $results (loss for every grid point tried, plus 'regional'/'nearest_block' reference rows)

functions.scaling_note: Offline, no network calls; seconds for a typical real dataset

functions.name: estimate_kernel_priors
functions.description: 2026-09-07, new -- the kernel-priors estimator itself. Site-centered distance-kernel weighting (geo x optional-covariate product kernel), replacing gridding + GLMM prediction entirely -- there is no create_sites_from_grid()/train_biodiversity_model() step in this path at all. Produces a priors object structurally compatible with the GLMM path's generate_full_priors() output (bind_rows()-compatible taxaexpect_priors), so every downstream consumer (join_priors(), generate_domestic_food_priors(), etc.) works unchanged regardless of which path produced it.

inputs.name: occurrence_data
inputs.description: Standardized occurrence data with lat/lon/main_habitat/taxon_name columns (std_occurrences)

inputs.name: site_lat
inputs.description: Focal site latitude

inputs.name: site_lon
inputs.description: Focal site longitude

inputs.name: site_habitat
inputs.description: Focal habitat (e.g. 'Marine')

inputs.name: lambda_km
inputs.description: Kernel bandwidth in km -- use calibrate_kernel_bandwidth()'s $best$lambda_km rather than guessing

inputs.name: m
inputs.description: Pseudo-record count for the regional back-off prior

inputs.name: covariate_col
inputs.description: Optional numeric covariate column (e.g. 'depth_m'); must match calibrate_kernel_bandwidth()'s own covariate_col if used

inputs.name: site_covariate
inputs.description: The focal site's own covariate value (e.g. mean depth of nearby records), required when covariate_col is supplied

inputs.name: lambda_covariate
inputs.description: Covariate-space bandwidth, from calibrate_kernel_bandwidth()'s $best$lambda_covariate

inputs.name: site_id
inputs.description: Site identifier stamped onto every output row (e.g. sprintf('Site_%.2f_%.2f', site_lat, site_lon)) -- used downstream as this path's grid_id equivalent

output.description: $priors (the taxaexpect_priors-shaped data frame: taxon_name, alpha, beta, theta_mean, theta_sd, prior_branch='resident_observed', effective_records), $params (incl. site_id), $n_eff, $missing_mass -- pass the WHOLE object (not just $priors) to generate_undetected_diversity()/generate_domestic_food_priors() as model_obj

functions.scaling_note: Offline, no network calls; seconds for a typical real dataset

functions.name: generate_undetected_diversity
functions.description: 2026-09-07, new -- unseen-taxa floor (Good-Turing/Chao-based dark-diversity mirrors) for the kernel-priors path, the kernel analog of what the GLMM path's generate_full_priors() computes internally. Output is bind_rows()-compatible with estimate_kernel_priors()'s own $priors.

inputs.name: model_obj
inputs.description: Output of estimate_kernel_priors() (the whole object, not just $priors)

inputs.name: jeffreys_threshold
inputs.description: Minimum singleton count before falling back to a Jeffreys-bounds floor

inputs.name: singleton_ess
inputs.description: Effective sample size assigned to each singleton mirror row

inputs.name: taxonomy
inputs.description: Occurrence data (e.g. the same std_occurrences fed to estimate_kernel_priors()) used to derive higher-rank taxonomy for the dark-diversity mirrors

output.description: Anonymous dark-diversity/undetected prior rows, prior_branch='resident_undetected', bind_rows()-compatible with estimate_kernel_priors()'s $priors

functions.name: apply_undetected_evidence
functions.description: 2026-09-07, new -- advanced/optional: elevates the dark-diversity floor for specific NAMED unobserved taxa using outside evidence (regional GBIF proximity just outside the study bbox, invasive/nonindigenous watch-list status, or iNaturalist range checks -- each its own evidence generator, e.g. generate_regional_proximity_evidence()/generate_invasive_watch_evidence()/generate_inat_range_evidence(), not covered by this entry). Metadata-only (no graph edge) -- this needs a real evidence table as input, which itself needs case-by-case design (a watch list, a regional-proximity search radius, etc.) rather than a one-size default; wire in directly if you have a specific evidence source, following the real production kernel-priors workflows' own pattern.

inputs.name: taxaexpect_priors
inputs.description: The priors table so far (e.g. estimate_kernel_priors()'s $priors + generate_undetected_diversity()'s output, already bind_rows()'d)

inputs.name: model_obj
inputs.description: Output of estimate_kernel_priors()

inputs.name: evidence
inputs.description: taxon_name + weight (+ p_conc) rows from an evidence generator -- see description

inputs.name: grid_id
inputs.description: Site id to elevate priors at (e.g. model_obj$params$site_id)

inputs.name: main_habitat
inputs.description: Habitat to stamp on elevated rows

inputs.name: taxonomy
inputs.description: Occurrence data for deriving elevated rows' higher-rank taxonomy

inputs.name: pricing
inputs.description: 'blend' (linear weight*ceiling) or 'curve' (per-sampling-group Good-Turing budget pricing)

output.description: Elevated prior rows for the named evidence taxa, bind_rows()-compatible with the rest of taxaexpect_priors

functions.scaling_note: Offline once the evidence table exists; the evidence generators themselves may make live GBIF/iNaturalist calls

functions.name: plot_theta_surface
functions.description: 2026-09-07, new -- the kernel-priors path's own visualizer (2026-09-01): a static (default) or optionally interactive KDE prior-field map for ONE taxon, evaluating estimate_kernel_priors()'s same estimator on a full grid via binned FFT convolution instead of at one site. Replaces plot_theta_map_interactive() for kernel priors, which parses Grid_<lat>_<lon> ids into centroids and has nothing to draw for a single opaque kernel site_id. Genuinely scriptable (interactive=FALSE is the default, a real static plot, not a Shiny gadget with no non-interactive path) -- unlike review_spatial_flags()/review_institution_flags()/review_spatial_context(), which have no non-interactive mode at all and so have no graph representation by design.

inputs.name: kernel_fit
inputs.description: Output of estimate_kernel_priors() (the whole object)

inputs.name: occurrence_data
inputs.description: The same standardized occurrence data fed to estimate_kernel_priors()

inputs.name: taxon
inputs.description: Which taxon_name to render the prior field for (one taxon per call)

inputs.name: n_grid
inputs.description: Grid resolution (n_grid x n_grid lattice)

inputs.name: covariate_at
inputs.description: Fixed covariate value to evaluate the surface at, if the kernel fit used one (e.g. a depth). Omitting it on a covariate-fit surface renders an explicitly labeled 'covariate omitted' map, never a silently wrong one

inputs.name: interactive
inputs.description: FALSE (default) renders a static base-R plot; TRUE renders an interactive leaflet map (requires leaflet)

output.description: A static plot (default) or leaflet htmlwidget (interactive=TRUE) of the prior field for the requested taxon

functions.scaling_note: ~1-2s per taxon for a 512x512 grid from ~1M occurrence records, after the shared kernel FFT is computed once per call
